definition: The Georgetown–IBM experiment was an influential demonstration of machine translation, which was performed on January 7, 1954.
details: Developed jointly by Georgetown University and IBM, the experiment involved completely automatic translation of more than sixty Russian sentences into English.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. And that is Georgetown–IBM experiment — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
